summary: Somchai Kusalacitto works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned a Ph.D. from the University of Madras and served as dean and deputy rector for foreign affairs at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (attested 2003).

Somdet Phra Nyanasamvara (1913–2013) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Wat Bowonniwet Vihara and under Swami Satyananda Puri and Vajirayanavangsa. He was abbot of Wat Bowonniwet Vihara (~1961–2013) and director at Mahamakut Buddhist University (1961).

Somphong Santacitto works in the field of Buddhist studies. He earned a master's degree in Buddhist studies at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University under the supervision of Phra Suthithammanuwat (attested 2006).

Sonam Chhoki works in Tibetology and history/archaeology. She completed an M.A. at Jawaharlal Nehru University and a Ph.D. at SOAS University of London, and worked as a history teacher at Samtse College of Education.
Sonam Choden specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She has been active at the University of Hamburg as a doctoral local researcher and scientific project staff member (attested 2026).

Sonam Gyatso (b. 1933) is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who taught Shinjo Kawasaki. He worked as a research assistant at Toyo Bunko (~1964–1978) and as a professor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2014).

Sonam Jamtsho specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied as a doctoral local researcher at the University of Hamburg, served there as a scientific project staff member (attested 2026), and taught Gembo Dorji.

Sonam Kachru specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under Dan Arnold and held posts including at the Max Planck Institute before becoming Assistant Professor at Yale University (attested 2026).

Sonam Kinga (b. 1973) is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Tibetology. He studied at Sherubtse College and Kyoto University, and served as a researcher at the Centre for Bhutan Studies and GNH (~1999–2007).

Sonam Thakchoe specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He earned a PhD at the University of Tasmania (~1999–2002) mentored by Jay L. Garfield and Jeff Malpas, and held a post there around 2003.

Sonam Tsering is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Supervised for his doctorate by Gray Tuttle and taught by several prominent scholars, he serves as Senior Lecturer and Director of the Tibetan Language Program at Columbia University (attested 2026).
Sondra L. Hausner specializes in religious studies and Indology. She serves as Professor of Anthropology of Religion at the University of Oxford and Wolfson College, Oxford (attested 2026).
Songeun Choe works in the fields of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Choe studied under master's supervisor Myung-dae Moon and doctoral supervisor Kiyohiko Munakata (attested 1991).

Sonja Arntzen (b. 1945) specializes in Japanology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of British Columbia (~1967–1979) under doctoral supervisor Leon Hurvitz, and also studied under Seizan Yanagida and Sojo Hirano.

Sonja Glauch (b. 1967) is a scholar of linguistics. She completed her Magister, Promotion, and Habilitation at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg, where she was an Akademische Oberrätin in 2007, and held visiting professorships in Vienna and Munich.

Sonya S. Lee specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history/archaeology. She completed a PhD at the University of Chicago under Hung Wu, taught at Swarthmore College (2003–2004), and held posts at Stanford University and the University of Southern California.

Soon-il Hwang works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed an MA at Dongguk University under Seung-won Seo, earned a DPhil at Mansfield College, Oxford, under Richard Gombrich, and served as an editorial board member at Dongguk University.

Soorakkulame Pemaratana specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at the National University of Singapore under thesis supervisor Saranindranath Tagore and serves as a visiting professor at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Sophus Bugge (1833–1907) was a Norwegian linguist who studied in Oslo, Copenhagen, and Berlin under Albrecht Weber. He was appointed Professor of Comparative Philology and Old Norse at the University of Oslo in 1866 and held a post at Uppsala (1877).
Soshu Nishioka is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who has served as a professor at Shitennoji University (attested 2000, 2015).
